answer: gfx942 uses FNUZ FP8, while gfx950 uses OCP FP8; the encodings are not bit-compatible, so weights must be re-quantized and revalidated.
gfx942 provides 64 KB of LDS with 32 banks; gfx950 provides 160 KB of LDS with 64 banks.
The CDNA3/CDNA4 ceiling is 32 waves/CU, derived from 8 wave slots per SIMD across four SIMDs.
gfx942 direct-to-LDS accepts at most a 4-byte transfer, while gfx950 adds 12-byte and 16-byte forms.
Native XF32 MFMA is unavailable on gfx950: the intrinsic fails to select and does not lower to a gfx950 matrix instruction.
gfx950 adds v_permlane16_swap_b32; that swap instruction is absent on gfx942, which needs a fallback such as DPP plus ds_bpermute.
Out-of-range raw buffer reads return zero, enabling branchless zero-fill when the descriptor bounds are correct.
The MI355X FP8 GEMM blog reports roughly 3500–4200 TFLOPS for large square M=N=K shapes such as 4096 or 8192. This is source-reported and unreproduced by the committed harness.
The current gfx942 guidance is compiler-checkable and source-backed, but MI300 runtime access was unavailable, so gfx942 remains compile-only rather than runtime-verified on MI300.
CDNA has no TMA or mbarrier equivalent. Use direct-to-LDS loads where applicable and order their completion with s_waitcnt.
